messages.text:
Fatras can be run to create the error parametrisation file as well - there's a script Digitzation/error_parameterization.py in ACTS for this.

If there's no 1-dim geometric digitization, switch to smearing digitization approach instead for the long strips - we will fix this later.

I’ll add the Fatras error-parameterization step using the ACTS script. For long strips, I’ll use geometric digitization if the corrected pilot produces valid 1D measurements; otherwise I’ll switch them to smearing and record that temporary choice.

The corrected Fatras pilot now produces both 1D long-strip and 2D pixel/short-strip measurements, so the smearing fallback is unnecessary. The independent 50,000-muon Fatras training sample is running.

Geant4 exposed a truth-association indexing bug and costly run initialization between events. SoftEng is addressing these in a task-local adapter, with explicit checks that event processing and physics remain unchanged.

The independent review confirmed a bug in the ACTS error-parameterization script: its final table entry stores an exact cluster-size width even when that entry is used for all larger clusters. I’ll retain the raw output and derive an audited overflow entry from the pooled training hits. Both backends will use the same frozen table.

The Geant4 lifecycle check passed: five identical-seed events produced exactly equal particles, hits, measurements and fitted-track data with the standard and persistent run managers. The persistent manager avoids repeated initialization. Fatras training is nearly complete; calibrated pilots and the six performance samples come next.

Fatras training completed with **699,273 measurements across all 52 sensitive volumes**. The audited error table is frozen, and both calibrated pilots are running against it. I’ll then collect 20,000 events for each of the six backend/momentum combinations.

Both calibrated pilots passed, including all seven sensor systems and exact checks that the written measurement variances match the frozen table. **All six production cases are now running.** The chain and training evidence are in [draft PR #101](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/101); I’ll add the performance results and independent assessment before marking it ready.

The independent reviewer reproduced all 106 error-table groups directly from the training ROOT file and found no blocking issue. The Fatras production cases are past halfway; all three Geant4 cases have completed initialization and are advancing through events.

The 3 T setup now has a frozen error table trained on an independent 50,000-muon Fatras sample. Native one-dimensional strip digitization works, so the long strips can stay geometric. All three Fatras performance samples have finished; the Geant4 samples are still running.

Fatras fitted 19,992, 19,998 and 19,999 of the 20,000 generated muons at 1, 10 and 100 GeV, respectively. The remaining events had fewer than seven unique measurements; every attempted fit succeeded. I’m preparing the retained results and plot replay while Geant4 finishes.

Two Geant4 runs crashed in the original ACTS truth finder, which was still running as a diagnostic beside the corrected finder used for fitting. I’ll remove that diagnostic path, retain the failed outputs, and rerun all six samples at one source revision. The simulation, digitization, error table and fitter settings will stay fixed.

The diagnostic path is removed, and all 24 controls pass in the native ACTS environment, including a check that the unsafe finder cannot be scheduled. All six replacement samples are running at the new fixed revision with the same trained error table.

The replacement runs are progressing normally. The analysis will retain selection losses, fit failures, non-Gaussian tails and non-unit pulls. Each final sample will also be checked against the frozen measurement-error table and the common executed source and binary hashes.

The three replacement Fatras samples have finished. Their generated particles and fitted tracks—including every stored covariance element—match the earlier completed runs exactly. Geant4 is in its final portion; next are the resolution and pull plots, followed by an independent review of the complete results.

All 120,000 performance events are complete. The reduction caught three fitted tracks with no native majority-particle match. I’m checking why they are unmatched so they remain accounted for and don’t silently disappear from the resolution results.

The three tracks failed ACTS’s requirement to retain at least half of the primary’s measurements. Each still has one verified primary-derived input candidate, so I’ll keep its residuals and pulls and count the native match failure separately. Across all six samples, four attempted fits failed; the native audit reports no invalid fitted covariance.

The profiles are ready. For central muons, the 68% relative-pT resolution is about 0.54–0.77% in Fatras and 0.79–1.16% in Geant4 across the three momenta. Pulls have substantial tails, especially in Geant4, and forward 100 GeV resolution degrades strongly. The report shows both central widths and full tail-sensitive statistics.

The results and ten figure sets are now in PR #101. The independent reviewer is checking the fixed source, ROOT data, matching safeguards, CSV and figures. I’m finishing the interaction records and exact closed-turn token accounting; the active coordinator turn remains excluded until it closes.

The reviewer has independently reproduced all measurement variances and 17,712 summary values from the ROOT files, and confirmed the fit losses and three unmatched cases. Figure and CSV checks are finishing. I’m also checking CI on the final PR head.

The independent review found no blocking implementation, analysis or presentation issue for this prototype. PR #101 is ready for human review, with usage and interaction records updated. The latest pushes did not schedule hosted checks automatically, so I’ll run the repository’s validation workflows explicitly before handing it back.

The final-head plotting and accounting checks passed. GitHub also reports a conflict with newer `main` changes. I’ll inspect and reconcile those changes, preserve the validated baseline, and rerun the required checks.

The conflict is resolved with both tracker studies and their records preserved. The validated baseline source, data and figures are byte-for-byte unchanged. The combined record validators, plot replay and propagation controls pass; I’m rerunning hosted checks on the merged branch.

Good start, I will need the full pull distributions:
(t_0^ture - t_0^re)/sigma_t_0 for all track paramters, integrated over all eta. Overlaying 1, 10, 100 GeV per track parameter

I’ll add full-range, all-η pull distributions using your **truth − reconstructed** convention, with 1, 10 and 100 GeV overlaid for each parameter and separate Geant4/Fatras panels. I’ll retain the tails and report underflow and overflow counts.

I’ll include all six ACTS bound parameters, plus derived pT. The time panel will be labeled as an unmeasured, prior-dependent diagnostic because this baseline has no timing response. The plots will include a full-range tail view and a conventional ±5 view, both normalized to all finite pulls.

All 119,982 fitted tracks enter every requested parameter histogram, with zero full-range underflow or overflow. The large tails remain visible. I’m checking the plot layout, then I’ll have the sign convention and bin counts reviewed independently against the ROOT data.

The full pull plots now include all six track parameters, with 1, 10, and 100 GeV overlaid for each simulation backend. I’m finishing the independent check of the sign convention, histogram counts, and tails before updating PR 101.

limitations: Only userMessage and agentMessage text retained; reasoning, tool arguments/results and private state excluded.
Conservative path, credential, email and URL redaction is not a privacy guarantee; review retained text.
Exposed operation counts are per retained turn; journal counts can describe the same invocations and must not be added.
